title: The neovim plugin installs from an nvim branch that CI keeps
body:
The neovim plugin lives in `editors/nvim/`, as `plugin/`, `ftdetect/`, `ftplugin/`, `syntax/`, `lua/acre/`, `tests/` and `README.md`. A plugin manager that installs from a git repo looks for those directories at the repo's root. Some managers can be pointed at a subdirectory. lazy.nvim cannot, and Jack uses it. A lazy user today has to clone acre and point `dir` at `editors/nvim`.

## Proposal

A GitHub Actions workflow keeps a branch named `nvim` whose root is `editors/nvim/`. A lazy user then installs the plugin with one line:

```lua
{ "jackroddy/acre", branch = "nvim" }
```

Nobody commits to `nvim` by hand. On each push that changes `editors/nvim/`, the workflow runs `git subtree split --prefix=editors/nvim` and pushes the result to `nvim`. The split produces the same commits from the same history, so each push fast-forwards `nvim`. `editors/nvim/` stays the place to edit the plugin, and to install it locally or by hand.

## Cost

- The repo has no `.github/` yet, so this adds the first workflow.
- The workflow needs `contents: write` to push `nvim`.
- The Branches section of `CLAUDE.md` says all work goes on `dev` and `main` carries releases. It would need to name `nvim` as a third branch that only the workflow writes.

## Open

- Which branch feeds `nvim`. Following `dev` gives lazy users each change as it lands. Following `main` gives them the plugin only at a release. The plugin and acre-gui talk over a socket, so a plugin newer than the user's acre-gui could send a message the viewer does not know. That argues for `main`.
- Whether a branch protection rule on `nvim` should refuse every push but the workflow's.
- `tests/` and `README.md` land on `nvim` with the rest. lazy ignores them, but the README's install section should then give the line above.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/cac6cd1d
notes.text:
Jack settled the open questions.

- `main` feeds `nvim`, so lazy users get the plugin at a release, in step with acre-gui.
- No branch protection on `nvim`. The branch is cheap to rewrite, so a stray push gets fixed by hand.
- The plugin's README gives the lazy line once the branch exists.

The costs listed are expected: the first workflow in the repo, and a line in the Branches section of `CLAUDE.md`. Once this lands, falx gets an issue that describes how to copy the setup.
